content.text: Hayden led a session on identifying business competitive advantages, focusing on systematic and data-driven approaches to maintain market leadership. The session, part of EMPOWER Labs Cohort 4, emphasized leveraging AI tools to monitor competitors, predict market shifts, and build defensible advantages. Participants were reminded that the transformation process allows for thorough planning, and the curriculum remains accessible after the program concludes next week. The session covered three main areas: using AI for competitor analysis, product or service expansions, and strategies for future-proofing and right-sizing businesses.

content.text: Hayden presented on AI's capabilities for analyzing industry trends, sizing markets, and identifying expansion opportunities. He demonstrated how AI can help businesses understand competitive landscapes, automate workflows, and optimize customer experiences. Hayden emphasized the importance of a staged approach to AI implementation and highlighted the potential for significant cost reductions in digital services. The session included a discussion about the balance between AI-driven insights and human judgment, with FM sharing her experience of working with an AI agency that recommended a large upfront investment. Hayden explained that true AI-first agencies still require human oversight and suggested that AI can enhance, rather than replace, human expertise in business operations.

content.text: Hayden discussed using AI tools like Claude and AI Studio to analyze data, create product roadmaps, and conduct cost-benefit analyses for business decisions. He emphasized the importance of systematic data collection and AI-driven approaches to improve decision-making processes. Hayden also shared insights into acquisition strategies, including tuck-ins and roll-ups, and highlighted the role of AI in evaluating capital allocation and go-to-market strategies.

content.text: Hayden explained how to create a GTM prompt within a master prompt project, emphasizing the importance of context and interaction with AI to prioritize acquisition channels and document processes. He highlighted the benefits of using AI as a tutor to map out processes, creating "capability install kits," which can be more effective than hiring consultants. Don shared his experience building a custom SQL database for tracking initiatives, replacing FileMaker, which took 48 hours to develop. The group discussed the potential for agencies to shift to a training and capability transfer model, and the value of AI in previewing future processes and cross-functional dependencies.

content.text: Don shared his experience building a database system using Supabase, which he created to manage leads and track opportunities from initial contact to sale. Hayden explained that Don's system provides CRM functionality and could potentially be enhanced with vector mappings to analyze data. Nancy discussed how AI might compete with her in-person English language school in Angola, and she considered using AI tools to enhance her students' learning experience through blended learning methods.

content.text: Hayden discussed the importance of building a strong brand and leveraging AI to create a competitive advantage. He suggested investing in brand development over the next 6-18 months, as the market will likely see a glut of content. Hayden emphasized the value of proprietary data and network effects in business, advising companies to explore these opportunities with the help of AI. He also suggested exploring switching costs and developing products that integrate deeply with customers' needs. Finally, Hayden highlighted the potential of using AI to tap into employees' knowledge and innovation, suggesting ways to collect and utilize this data to improve business processes and create new ideas.

content.text: Hayden discussed the concept of mining employees' capabilities and mentioned a Teams program for custom cohorts. He emphasized the importance of right-sizing strategies based on business stage, such as focusing on single product market fit for startups and longer development cycles for growing businesses. Hayden also clarified that new product service development would be considered R&D, while testing new acquisition channels would be part of marketing spend. He stressed the need to allocate time and resources to AI-enable teams, comparing it to building an economy in resource management games.

content.text: The group discussed their AI usage and time allocation, with FM reporting that AI occupies 50% of his workday across coaching, experimentation, and implementing AI processes with his engineering team. Beni shared that while he increased his AI usage since joining the cohort, he still needs to allocate more time to fully leverage AI capabilities, particularly for decision-making and business model innovation. Hayden emphasized the importance of dedicated time for learning and experimentation, sharing his own experience of regaining his edge by returning to learning cloud code after a period of focusing on other tasks. The discussion concluded with Nancy reflecting on her journey through multiple cohorts, finding value in the structured approach and iterative process of AI adoption, while Hayden recommended that participants install Cloud Code or Codex as their next step in AI development.

content.text: Hayden demonstrated how to use Cloud Code with Obsidian for note-taking and organization, emphasizing its flexibility compared to Notion. He explained the process of setting up directories for different aspects of business management and using Cloud Code to navigate and search these folders. Hayden also discussed the integration of Cloud Code with Notebook LM for tasks like creating mind maps and presentations. The group discussed security concerns related to using Cloud Code, with Hayden clarifying that there are no significant differences between using the app and terminal versions. Hayden announced the next session would be on Monday, with office hours on Friday, and encouraged participants to complete optional homework tasks related to process development.
